cards.v: A second likewise is this, ‘You shall love your neighbor as yourself.’
cards.a: Today treat one person the way you hope to be treated: greet first, give up your seat first, say thank you first.

cards.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger;
cards.a: Put your phone down and listen to someone for five full minutes—no interrupting, no rushing to advise.

cards.v: Let no corrupt speech proceed out of your mouth, but only what is good for building others up as the need may be, that it may give grace to those who hear.
cards.a: Send a friend one specific word of encouragement: “I really appreciate how you…”

cards.v: Don’t forget to show hospitality to strangers, for in doing so, some have entertained angels without knowing it.
cards.a: Invite someone new—or someone you haven’t seen in a long time—for tea or a simple meal.

cards.v: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
cards.a: Celebrate a friend’s good news wholeheartedly—without adding “Me too…”

cards.v: Rejoice with those who rejoice. Weep with those who weep.
cards.a: Call or visit someone who is struggling. Stay with them; don’t rush to explain or fix.

cards.v: leave your gift there before the altar, and go your way. First be reconciled to your brother, and then come and offer your gift.
cards.a: Think of someone you have friction with. Pray for them, then take one small step toward peace.

cards.v: He who covers an offense promotes love; but he who repeats a matter separates best friends.
cards.a: When you hear gossip in conversation or a group chat today, choose not to pass it on or add to it.

cards.v: He who has pity on the poor lends to the LORD; he will reward him.
cards.a: Prepare one practical help for someone in need: a meal, some daily supplies, or your time.

cards.t: Seek the Peace of the City
cards.v: Seek the peace of the city where I have caused you to be carried away captive, and pray to the LORD for it; for in its peace you will have peace.”
cards.a: Pray for your neighborhood, building, or street—and learn one neighbor’s name.

cards.v: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
cards.a: Write down one old debt you are holding, and tell the Lord, “Lord, I choose to forgive.”

cards.v: And be kind to one another, tender hearted, forgiving each other, just as God also in Christ forgave you.
cards.a: Give heartfelt thanks to someone who serves you—a cashier, a driver, a cleaner.

cards.v: Pleasant words are a honeycomb, sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.
cards.a: When a family member or coworker finishes a task, name the specific good you noticed.

cards.t: A Friend Loves at All Times
cards.v: A friend loves at all times; and a brother is born for adversity.
cards.a: Reach out to a friend who has been low lately: “I was thinking of you—how are you doing?”

cards.v: A gentle answer turns away wrath, but a harsh word stirs up anger.
cards.a: The next time you are provoked, pause three seconds, breathe, and answer softly.

cards.v: doing nothing through rivalry or through conceit, but in humility, each counting others better than himself;
cards.a: In a gathering or discussion, give someone else the chance to speak—or the credit.

cards.v: each of you not just looking to his own things, but each of you also to the things of others.
cards.a: Remember what a friend is facing, and ask how it is going next week.

cards.v: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.
cards.a: Greet someone who is being left out or new in the room, and talk with them for a while.

cards.v: Let your speech always be with grace, seasoned with salt, that you may know how you ought to answer each one.
cards.a: Before posting a comment online, ask: Is this gracious? Will it build someone up?

cards.v: Even so, let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your Father who is in heaven.
cards.a: Quietly do one good thing today—not to be seen, but so that God gets the glory.

cards.t: Pray for Those Who Hurt You
cards.v: But I tell you, love your enemies, bless those who curse you, do good to those who hate you, and pray for those who mistreat you and persecute you,
cards.a: Sincerely pray a blessing over someone who has hurt you or whom you dislike.

cards.v: Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfill the law of Christ.
cards.a: Ask a friend, “Is there anything I can do for you?”—and then do it.

cards.v: Day by day, continuing steadfastly with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they took their food with gladness and singleness of heart,
cards.a: Have a phone-free meal with family or friends, and share what you are thankful for this week.

cards.v: Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend’s countenance.
cards.a: Meet a spiritual companion, share one struggle each, and pray for each other.

cards.v: redeeming the time, because the days are evil.
cards.a: Turn off your phone for one hour tonight and give that time to God and the people near you.

cards.v: but speaking truth in love, we may grow up in all things into him who is the head, Christ,
cards.a: There is a true word you have been avoiding. Pray first, then say it gently.

cards.v: Repay no one evil for evil. Respect what is honorable in the sight of all men.
cards.a: When someone is rude to you, choose not to snap back; answer with kindness.

cards.v: Likewise, you younger ones, be subject to the elder. Yes, all of you clothe yourselves with humility and subject yourselves to one another; for “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”
cards.a: Admit you were wrong about something small today, and say “I’m sorry.”

cards.v: Walk in wisdom toward those who are outside, redeeming the time.
cards.a: Pray for one of your Five Names, and do one caring thing for them.

cards.v: A new commandment I give to you, that you love one another. Just as I have loved you, you also love one another.
cards.a: Write a card or message to someone you love, telling them the grace of God you see in them.

recon.safety: If this involves violence, domestic abuse, sexual harassment or assault, stalking, fraud, extortion, bullying, threats, or any crime, please do not face it alone, and you do not need to “go privately” first. Make sure you are safe, reach out to a trusted person, pastor, or professional service, and contact the police when needed. Forgiveness is not silence, and reconciliation never means returning to danger.

steps.v: Why do you see the speck that is in your brother’s eye, but don’t consider the beam that is in your own eye? Or how will you tell your brother, ‘Let me remove the speck from your eye,’ and behold, the beam is in your own eye? You hypocrite! First remove the beam out of your own eye, and then you can see clearly to remove the speck out of your brother’s eye.
steps.d: Remove the log from your own eye first. What is my part in this? How much pride, hurt, or judgment is in my heart?
q: What is my part in this?
Do I want to win this person—or win the argument?

steps.v: So, then, my beloved brothers, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, and slow to anger; for the anger of man doesn’t produce the righteousness of God.
steps.d: Be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger. Give it at least one night. Bring your emotions and your own wrongs to the Lord, and ask the Spirit to govern your heart and mouth.
q: What do I need to confess to God?
Am I willing to pray a blessing over them?
What is the Spirit reminding me of?

steps.v: “If your brother sins against you, go, show him his fault between you and him alone. If he listens to you, you have gained back your brother.
steps.d: When it is just the two of you, speak humbly, specifically, and without accusation. Apologize for your part first, then share how you felt. The goal is to win the person.
q: Can I apologize for my part first?
What is the one specific thing I need to say?
Am I ready to listen to their side?

steps.v: But if he doesn’t listen, take one or two more with you, that at the mouth of two or three witnesses every word may be established.
steps.d: If they will not talk, ask one or two mature, fair people whom you both trust to come along—not to gang up, but to help you both see clearly.
q: Who do both of us trust?
Have I sincerely completed the previous step?

steps.v: If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.
steps.d: If it is still unresolved, go through an appropriate formal channel (a pastor, community mediation, a supervisor, professional help)—not group chats or whispers. “If it is possible, as much as it is up to you, be at peace with all men.”
q: Am I using the right channel?

steps.v: bearing with one another, and forgiving each other, if any man has a complaint against any; even as Christ forgave you, so you also do.
steps.d: Forgiveness lays down the right to collect the debt and leaves judgment to God. Trust can be rebuilt over time as there is real change. When needed, you can forgive and still keep a safe distance.
q: Am I willing to say, “Lord, I choose to forgive”?
What healthy boundary do I need?

opens: I want to apologize for my part first: …
I care about our relationship, so I’d like to talk with you about something.
When … happened, I felt … . I’d like to hear your side.
I may have misunderstood you—could you help me understand?
Thank you for hearing me out. Could we work this out together?

fruits.d: Loving those who are hard to love
Glad for others’ good, without comparing
Governing my tongue, temper, and phone

way.t: The Holy Spirit is my guide
way.q: Before meeting this person, have I asked the Holy Spirit?
How does Scripture tell me to treat them?
How would Jesus love this person?
Am I relying on the Lord’s love or on my own social skills?

way.t: Let Jesus receive all the glory
way.q: Who gets the glory for the fruit of this relationship?

five.intro: Write down five friends, family members, coworkers, or neighbors who don’t yet know the Lord. Pray for one each day, and do one loving thing for one of them each month. Friendship has value in itself; the gospel is love’s natural overflow. No pressure, and no one is a project.

steps.d: Pray for them daily; ask the Lord to open their heart.
Remember their birthday, needs, and struggles.
Eat, exercise, and work alongside them; be part of their life.
At the right time, tell them of God’s grace in your life.
Invite them to a meal, a Bible study, a gospel event, or fellowship.
When they want to know the Lord, walk the first stretch of faith with them.

prays.p: Lord, open their heart, as you opened Lydia’s.
God who said, “Light will shine out of darkness,” shine in their heart.
Open a door for the word, and give me the right words.
Lord of the harvest, send workers to them—and use me.
Tell God the desire of my heart: that they may be saved.

tips: It doesn’t have to be perfect: a bowl of noodles or a pot of tea is enough—your heart is what matters.
Pray for your guests first: ask the Lord to make this time a doorway of grace.
Remember their name and one thing they care about.
Ask more, listen more; let them talk more than you do.
Put your phone away so they feel valued.
Use wisdom and boundaries: be careful about being alone with someone of the opposite sex, late nights, or meeting strangers from online.
Look after the overlooked: give the quietest person a chance to speak.
Close with a word of blessing, then send a thank-you message afterward.

checks: My phone is the first thing I check in the morning and the last thing at night.
I often look at my phone while eating or talking with people.
After seeing others’ updates, I often feel I’m not good enough.
I care about likes, or about messages left on read.
I have said things online I would never say face to face.
I have forwarded news without checking whether it was true.
I scroll to escape loneliness, anxiety, or boredom.
I spend less time in the Word and prayer than on social media.
tips: Set aside a weekly digital Sabbath: turn off notifications and return to God and the people near you.
When you wake up, pray and read one verse before you open your phone.
Put your phone out of sight during meals.
Before posting, commenting, or forwarding, ask: Is it true? Is it gracious? Will it build up?
Unfollow accounts that keep you comparing or unsettled.
Each day, use your phone to bless one person: a greeting, a thank-you.
